source_bindings.interpretation: Previously reviewed frozen R14 sources, bound by implementation-ready and source qualification; no new source mutation.

required_comparisons.baseline: qualified R14 runtime, all MALLOC_* and GLIBC_TUNABLES absent
required_comparisons.candidate: the identical R14 runtime SHA, MALLOC_ARENA_MAX=1 and other allocator controls absent
required_comparisons.attribution: Controlled allocator configuration comparison within this finite ABBA campaign.
required_comparisons.guard: A and B executable SHA must both equal 51480b3cf630a95419d3afeb571eec17c90cffa5944101920d05333673de031d.

required_comparisons.baseline: qualified R11 runtime with clean allocator environment
required_comparisons.candidate: qualified R14 runtime with arena1 execution profile
required_comparisons.attribution: Combined code plus configuration outcome versus R11, not an isolated allocator effect.

no_cross_campaign_pooling: Keep each comparison's raw calls, CPU, wall durations and percentiles separate. Do not multiply percentage gains across campaigns or label R11-to-final as allocator-only improvement.

cancellation_report.fixture: Escaped JSON receipt; 8 expected wrong-host cancellation refusals plus one successful host_list per wave. Not successful remote cancellation throughput.
arm_columns: actual binary SHA and environment fingerprint
two process identities and both raw values
VmHWM after: both samples and median
VmRSS before and after: both samples and median
cancellation_report.aggregation: CPU_ms=1000*sum(measured controller CPU)/sum(measured mixed replies). Rate=sum(measured mixed replies)/sum(measured wall). Percentiles pool all measured raw latencies within one arm/case/tool and use nearest rank ceil(p*N). Never average per-process p95 or take median rates as the primary metric.
cancellation_report.warmup: Exclude two warmup waves from formal CPU/wall/latency denominators. The earlier allocator diagnostics included warmup and must remain separately labeled.
cancellation_report.p99_resolution: With 48 host_list samples per arm/case, nearest-rank p99 is the maximum; with 384 cancellation samples it is sorted rank 381. These are weak finite-tail summaries, not stable population tail estimates.
cancellation_report.memory_scope: VmHWM is whole child since exec, including initialize and warmup; not request incremental memory. VmRSS before/after is a point sample, not an RSS peak or a 12-second idle reading. Keep all missing/error values; no conversion of unavailable to zero.
cancellation_report.source_gap: Frozen cancel analyzer emits p95 and HWM; independent reporting may compute p99 and RSS before/after from retained raw records without changing the measurement code.

native_report.host_tool_balance: Six original jobs; equal process_status and process_read counts for every host.
arm_columns: per-host/tool distributions if a concrete regression needs localization
native_report.aggregation: Pool only raw measured calls within an arm/concurrency; rate=sum(calls)/sum(seconds), CPU=1000*sum(synchronous same-PID/start-ticks CPU deltas)/sum(calls). Do not use sampled tree CPU as performance numerator. Exclude warmup, preflight and restart checks.
native_report.p99_resolution: At 192 measured calls per arm/C, nearest-rank p99 is sorted rank 191; one or two tail samples can move it materially.
native_report.memory_scope: Report first-controller whole-lifetime kernel VmHWM and sampled VmRSS peak, each with both process samples/median. This spans preflight, warmup and all C1/C4/C8 cells, so it is not per-C or per-call memory. Report restart controller separately. Tree RSS/fd are nonsimultaneous sampled sums; controller RSS peak is a sampled lower bound, not an exact global peak.
native_report.metric_errors: Retain metric_sample counts and FD/permission errors. Zero with zero samples is unavailable. Missing FD does not erase independently available CPU/RSS. Sampled tree CPU endpoint error can have either sign.
native_report.response_proof_scope: Native observation rows retain DTO/response hashes and validation flags, not all JSON-RPC bodies; do not claim independent transport-envelope rehash. Recovery has separate retained full reply evidence.

qualification_and_recovery_report.qualification: Bind unchanged 219 R14 compile inputs, retained artifact SHA, selected arena1, exact passed/failed/ignored identities and zero retries. R14 expected inventory is 1670 selected/1637 pass/33 ignored; actual R15 result remains pending.
qualification_and_recovery_report.environment: Report all explicit Popen environments, verified versus unavailable_process_exited counts; preferably separate listing commands from actual tests. At least one live observation is a gate, not a claim that all short tests were live-observed. Top-level isolated metadata binary_sha is null; per-test executable SHA and original inventory/audit chain carry the binary binding.
qualification_and_recovery_report.native_environment: Two live environment observations per ABBA round (first and normal restart), eight per complete native campaign; cancel has one per process.
qualification_and_recovery_report.recovery_environment: Exactly three controller starts: first, after intentional controller crash, after successful cancellation/restart; all must show selected env and unchanged held SSH agent.
qualification_and_recovery_report.recovery: Validate six owned new jobs, same-key reuse, concurrent cancellation, persisted receipts/output/exit witnesses, independent SSH readback and zero automatic retries. Signal ACK with termination_confirmed=false is not terminal proof; later status/exit/witness establishes termination.
qualification_and_recovery_report.limits: Controlled controller crash/restart and owned transport interruption do not establish physical power-loss durability, target reboot safety or arbitrary WAN partition/failover coverage.

factual_observations: R14 build-preflight records four logical CPUs. The parent task identifies this X230 as two physical cores; logical CPU time must not be confused with physical core throughput.

In the already audited large-refusal campaign, R14 used about 1.96 logical CPU-seconds per wall-second, versus 3.32-3.38 for R13. Rate fell 14.33-19.45%, CPU/RPC fell 28.14-30.83%, host_list p95 fell 57.20-58.00%, while cancellation p95 rose 12.10-32.30%.
Those refusal cases stop before cancellation audit-intent append or remote dispatch. They do not directly demonstrate waiting on the successful cancellation fsync path.

R14 preparation=2 includes synchronous prepare plus durable append, releases at true closure exit, and does not span remote/completion waits. Publication remains 8. Native read-only status/read does not acquire this cancellation preparation semaphore.
Arena diagnostics removed most retained RSS without reducing observed thread peak; R15 Rust remains exactly R14.

frontier_assessment.recommendation_if_formal_r15_is_good: Accept arena1/preparation2 as a measured engineering stopping point if qualification/recovery pass and all formal tradeoffs are acceptable. Do not automatically expand the parameter matrix. This is not a proof of global or even preparation-count Pareto optimality.

preparation_2_to_4.proven: No arena1/preparation4 candidate has been measured. Two physical cores alone cannot prove preparation4 useless, especially with four logical CPUs.
preparation_2_to_4.plausible_upside: Four preparations could use SMT or overlap actual filesystem/append waits and recover part of the observed cancellation rate loss. This is a concrete hypothesis, not a predicted gain.
preparation_2_to_4.evidence_against_automatic_test: Current large refusal data already uses about two logical CPUs continuously. It does not show an obvious idle CPU gap that a larger prep bound would fill. The observed preparation8-to2 exchange bought substantial CPU and host_list responsiveness at the cost of refusal rate and cancellation tail.
preparation_2_to_4.plausible_costs: More simultaneous large input/scratch buffers can raise transient HWM even with one arena; one allocator arena can add contention; more CPU/scheduler/SMT competition may give back CPU efficiency or host_list latency. None of these tradeoffs is measured for preparation4.
preparation_2_to_4.when_worth_revisiting: Only if final formal evidence leaves a concrete throughput or tail objective unmet and evidence localizes it to cancellation preparation rather than native read-only work. Then a separately qualified, bounded preparation4 comparison with the same selected allocator is appropriate.
preparation_2_to_4.validation_required: A new source candidate and ownership/queue/cancel/panic qualification are required; retain publication8, physical guard lifetime, cancelled queued work ownership and all public-entry assertions. Do not simply relabel the preparation2 tests or silently change the tested bound.
preparation_2_to_4.not_a_reason: Do not test solely because 4 is an untried parameter or because allocator arenas and preparation workers share numeric labels.

arena2_trigger.proceed_only_if: The same-binary arena1 campaign shows a coherent material C8 cost across both B processes relative to both A processes, preferably with higher CPU/call and lower rate/tail degradation rather than a lone p99 outlier. Compare individual process spread and shared-host conditions; two runs do not prove significance.
arena2_trigger.next_step_if_triggered: Use a targeted arena1-versus2 comparison of the affected native dimension with the same binary, explicit environments and retained negatives. Do not rerun an entire matrix by default.
arena2_trigger.inference_limit: Performance evidence can be consistent with allocator contention without proving its lock-level mechanism. Avoid claiming measured futex contention when no such trace was collected.

deferred_options.reason: Arena1 directly targets the demonstrated retention without new Rust scheduling semantics. A two-level dedicated-worker design adds threads/handoffs and requires panic, partial initialization, queued ownership and Tokio graceful-shutdown evidence. No demonstrated remaining benefit yet.

deferred_options.option: Cross-call pin cache or skip complete content rehash
deferred_options.reason: Existing phase-boundary change detection depends on content revalidation. Metadata/inode/mtime reuse is not equivalent; eliminating checks changes the contract rather than being a safe local speedup.

The current ValidatedJobString visitor already discards decoded text without a second String copy. A new scanner/parser requires independent Unicode, escaping, malformed-input and refusal equivalence evidence; there is no simple duplicate-copy fix left.
Requires a separate consistency, ownership, pin and recovery design with new correctness evidence; not a low-risk continuation of the current allocator setting change.
Would change persistence or cancellation safety semantics and does not explain the wrong-host benchmark hot path, which rejects before intent append.

frontier_assessment.statement_for_final_report: The optimization stops at a validated resource/throughput tradeoff under the measured X230 workloads. Preparation4, larger protocol changes and other allocators remain untested; absolute optimality is not established.
